decisions.decision: The Firestore client contract is settled by measurement, not by reading: for a query ordered by firestore.DocumentID, a STRING cursor value passed to StartAfter must be the document id RELATIVE TO THE QUERIED COLLECTION, never a path. The client prefixes the collection's own full resource name itself. Measured against the local emulator at a258ed2 with cloud.google.com/go/firestore v1.25.0: StartAfter(collectionPath + slash + docID) returns InvalidArgument, with the server naming a parent whose installations/.../requirements segment pair appears TWICE and reporting that it lacks a slash at index 203; StartAfter(docID) returns OK with 4 of 5 rows; StartAfter(the last snapshot's *DocumentRef) returns OK with the identical 4 rows; StartAfter(the *DocumentSnapshot) returns OK with the identical 4 rows. The route-level reproduction is the same failure: Service.ListRequirementsPage over the emulator returns page 1 with next_cursor eyJ2IjoidjEiLCJhZnRlciI6InJlcXVpcmVtZW50LTEifQ, and the very next call with that cursor returns that same InvalidArgument.
decisions.rationale: The reported cause is confirmed and the mechanism is in the client's own source rather than in the emulator: Query.fieldValuesToCursorValues (query.go, v1.25.0) switches on the cursor value's type and, for a string under an isDocumentID order, builds ReferenceValue as q.path + slash + docID, where q.path is the FULL resource name of the collection (CollectionRef.Path, measured as projects/agentic-loop-test/databases/(default)/documents/installations/<installation-key>/requirements). StartAt's own doc comment states the rule outright: 'If an OrderBy call uses the special DocumentID field path, the corresponding value should be the document ID relative to the query's collection.' So internal/store/firestore/store.go was doing the client's prefixing a second time, and the doubled parent is exactly what the server rejected. Settling this by measurement matters because the same defect is invisible in code review -- the expression reads as 'the document's path', which is a true description of a value the API does not want.

decisions.decision: Take the bare collection-relative document id, and take it through ONE named helper rather than two open-coded expressions. Add one unexported function in internal/store/firestore/store.go -- name it documentIDCursor(afterID string) (string, error) -- that returns PathKey(afterID) and carries a doc comment stating the client contract from d1 verbatim, naming the InvalidArgument it replaces. Both paged reads call it. Reject the *DocumentRef form and reject the *DocumentSnapshot form.
decisions.rationale: Three measured reasons for rejecting the two alternatives, and one for the helper. (a) The *DocumentRef form is the WEAKER guard, not the stronger one: measured, StartAfter given a *DocumentRef belonging to a DIFFERENT collection of the same installation was silently ACCEPTED and returned all 5 rows -- the whole unfiltered page -- because the client's own source carries an unimplemented 'TODO(jba): error if document ref does not belong to the right collection' at that exact branch. The snapshot branch, by contrast, does check the parent. Choosing the ref form would trade a loud failure for a silent full-page reset. (b) The *DocumentSnapshot form is checked but costs a read this page does not otherwise make, of a document that a caller's cursor may name and the collection may no longer hold; the page would then have to decide between an error and a restart, which is a new decision the outcome does not ask for. (c) The bare string is the client's documented contract, needs no extra read, and is a one-token deletion. The helper exists because the defect's real shape is 'two call sites open-coded the same translation and both got it wrong'; a single named translation with the contract written above it is what stops the third paged read from getting it wrong again.

decisions.decision: The layering is already right and does not change: the route returns an opaque cursor and the store is the sole owner of translating it into its own key space. Measured, the client's internal representation does NOT leak into what the route hands out -- the cursor decodes to the JSON object {v: v1, after: requirement-1}, carrying the DOMAIN Requirement id and no collection path, no base64 document-id encoding and no adapter detail of any kind. application.encodeCursor/decodeCursor own the envelope; internal/application/ports.go already states the contract correctly ('afterID is an internal, stable ordering key; the public service wraps it in an opaque cursor'). Therefore the bytes the route returns are IDENTICAL before and after this change, and internal/application/** stays prohibited.
decisions.rationale: This is what makes the non-goal 'do not change what the route returns to make a broken cursor look accepted' structurally satisfied rather than merely promised: there is nothing to change on the producing side, because the producing side was never wrong. The defect was entirely inside the one adapter that translates the port's key into its own document key, which is precisely the layer that is allowed to know about document ids. Stating the measured non-leak is also what forecloses the tempting wrong fix -- putting the encoded Firestore document id into the cursor envelope, which would make the cursor adapter-specific and break the memory adapter and every replay of a stored cursor.

decisions.decision: The in-memory adapter is passing because it is self-consistent, NOT by accident, so it gets no behavioural change -- and the reason must be recorded precisely, because the two adapters do NOT share one total order and a test that assumes they do would be wrong in a way that looks right. Memory sorts by the raw domain id and advances with rows[start].ID.String() <= afterID (internal/store/memory/store.go:208-227), an exclusive-after over raw-id lexicographic order. Firestore sorts by the document id, which is PathKey(rawID) = base64url(rawID), and after d2 advances by that same encoded key: also an exclusive-after, over a DIFFERENT total order. Measured, base64url is not order-preserving: brute-forcing the two-character suffix of req-XX over the full 64-character base64url alphabet found 724992 inverted pairs, for instance raw req-aa < req-at while encoded cmVxLWFh > cmVxLWF0.
decisions.rationale: Both adapters satisfy the port's actual promise -- a stable total order plus exclusive-after over the very key the caller was handed -- and that promise, not a shared order, is what the outcome needs: it is exactly what makes the concatenation of pages cover every record once. So memory needs no fix. But the consequence for the acceptance is decisive: the same-named cross-adapter test must NOT assert that a page is sorted by raw Requirement id, because that assertion passes on memory and fails on Firestore for a reason that has nothing to do with the cursor, and an implementer who hits that red will 'fix' it by weakening the walk. Two further measured consequences are recorded and deliberately not acted on: internal/application/allocation.go:603 and internal/application/release_surface.go:265 take the FIRST page of RequirementsPage, so which Requirements a scheduler pass considers differs between the two adapters -- a pre-existing divergence, outside this outcome, and a candidate for its own task.

decisions.decision: The outcome is fixed by ONE test name present in BOTH adapter packages, and it walks to exhaustion rather than one hop. The name is TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce, in internal/store/firestore/store_test.go and in internal/store/memory/store_test.go. Each drives the SAME sequence over its own adapter: seed N Requirements with N strictly greater than 3, call Service.ListRequirementsPage with page_size 1, then feed each returned next_cursor into the next call until a page returns no cursor; assert every page except possibly the last is exactly page_size rows, assert the terminal page carries no cursor, and assert the concatenation of all pages equals the seeded set with NO duplicate and NO omission, judged as a multiset. Then repeat the whole walk at a second page size that does not divide N and assert the same set. Assert nothing about the order the ids arrive in. The EventsPage counterpart is TestTheEventPageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryEventIsCoveredOnce, same two packages, same shape.
decisions.rationale: A single round trip would pass on a fix that only repairs the first hop -- for example one that special-cased the first page -- and would not see a cursor that is accepted but positions wrongly. Coverage-as-a-multiset is the assertion that actually carries the outcome: it fails on refusal, it fails on a duplicated row, it fails on a skipped row, and it fails on a walk that never terminates, all without naming an order. The second walk at a non-dividing page size is what catches an off-by-one in the exclusive boundary, which is the classic way a cursor 'works' while losing exactly one record per page. Driving it through Service.ListRequirementsPage rather than through the port directly is deliberate: the outcome is stated about the cursor the ROUTE returns, so the test must exercise the encode/decode envelope, not just the adapter.

decisions.decision: The route-level proof against real persistence is EXECUTABLE and must be executed: extend TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive in internal/api/live_local_test.go, which already starts the real cmd/control-plane binary against the real Firestore emulator over real HTTP and requires no Provider at all. It captures at least 3 Requirements, then pages GET /v1/requirements with page_size=1, feeding back each next_cursor until a page returns none, and asserts every captured id appears exactly once across the walk. Its argv is: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api.
decisions.rationale: This is what turns 'a cursor the route just returned is accepted by the next request' from a claim about a store method into an observed HTTP fact, at the same layer the M5 dogfood measured the defect, without spending a Provider invocation. It is measurably reachable to the implementer: the test is gated only on AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 plus FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, it builds cmd/control-plane itself, and it already issues GET /v1/requirements?page_size=25 at internal/api/live_local_test.go:231. Because this proof exists, the Provider-gated dogfood is NOT the only route-level evidence, and the task does not need to claim an execution it cannot perform.

decisions.decision: Refusal must not be weakened, and the way that is enforced is a POSITIVE test of the refusals rather than a promise. Measured, what is rejected today and where: application.decodeCursor (internal/application/readmodels.go:35-51) returns ErrInvalidCursor for a value that is not base64url, for decoded bytes over 1024, for invalid UTF-8, for JSON that does not parse, for a version that is not v1, for an empty after, for an after over 512 characters and for a whitespace-only after; PathKey (internal/store/firestore/store.go:183-191) rejects an empty or invalid-UTF-8 or over-MaxPathKeyBytes key. None of that changes. A new test named TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue asserts that a fabricated cursor, a cursor whose envelope version is not v1, a truncated prefix of a real cursor, and a cursor from a different collection's key space (a well-formed envelope carrying an Increment id) each still produce 400 with code invalid_request, in the SAME change that makes a real cursor work.
decisions.rationale: The instruction that no fix may move toward 'accept everything' is only credible if the refusals are asserted rather than left to be observed by absence. Two measured facts shape what that test may claim. First, a well-formed envelope carrying an id that does not exist is NOT an error today and must not become one: measured, StartAfter with a fabricated document id returns OK with 0 rows, and the memory adapter returns the page positioned after that key -- so 'a cursor from another collection' is testable at the ROUTE only if the envelope itself is what rejects it, which for a truncated or mis-versioned cursor it is. Second, and recorded rather than fixed: the 400 the dogfood saw did not come from cursor validation at all. internal/api's domainError (api.go:1116-1128) DEFAULTS to 400 invalid_request for any error it does not classify, so a storage-side gRPC InvalidArgument was dressed as a caller mistake. That masking is why a server bug read as a bad cursor for three exercises. Changing the default status would alter the response of every route in the file and is squarely outside this outcome; it is escalated to the coordinator as its own task, and the mitigation here is that after d2 no storage InvalidArgument is produced on this path at all.

decisions.decision: The same defect exists in exactly one other paged read, and it is fixed in the SAME task rather than deferred. Measured, the whole tree contains exactly three StartAfter call sites, all in internal/store/firestore/store.go: :633 in RequirementsPage and :763 in EventsPage, both defective with the identical doubled-prefix expression, and :957 in ExpiredActiveLeases, which is CORRECT because it passes last.Ref.ID -- a bare document id -- as the second of two cursor values, and whose round trip is already covered by internal/store/firestore/store_test.go:316-326. EventsPage's failure was reproduced, not inferred: EventsPage(ctx, first page's event id, 10) against the emulator returns 0 rows and the same InvalidArgument naming a doubled events parent. Every other bounded read takes no cursor and only reports truncation: ActiveLeases (:995), the pending control-verification scan (:1043), the links-by-repository scan (:1496), the publication-observation scan (:1577), the outbox candidate scan (:1918) and readCollection (:2171).
decisions.rationale: Splitting them would be worse on every axis: they are two lines of the same file inside one component, they call the same new helper, they are covered by the same test shape, and EventsPage's port doc (internal/application/ports.go:130) makes the same promise RequirementsPage does, so leaving it would leave a second cursor that the next task discovers the same way. The second victim is what settles it: internal/reconciler/orphan.go:54 feeds the raw Requirement id of the previous batch's last row back into RequirementsPage (orphan.go:58-60), so against a real Firestore the OrphanSweep cannot advance past its first batch of MaxBatch -- and its own test TestOrphanSweepIsCursorPagedAndBounded passes only because internal/reconciler tests run on the memory adapter. Fixing RequirementsPage repairs the sweep without editing internal/reconciler, which stays prohibited.

decisions.decision: No Firestore index is created and firestore.indexes.json is not touched. Measured: the fixed query is a single-collection query ordered only by DocumentID, which the emulator served with no index declaration present, and the fix changes only the cursor VALUE, never the query's shape, its filters or its ordering. If an implementer finds an index necessary, that means the query changed and the design was departed from: stop and escalate.
decisions.rationale: Making this an explicit prohibition rather than a silence is the guard the instruction asks for. An added index would be the visible symptom of the wrong fix -- for instance ordering by a stored requirement-id field in order to make the two adapters share one total order, which is a different and much larger design (it changes read cost, it needs a written field on every existing document, and it needs a migration for documents already stored). Nothing in this outcome requires the adapters to share an order (d4), so nothing in it requires an index.

decisions.decision: cap-backlog-visibility becomes demonstrable by this task, and an M5 re-dogfood is REQUIRED and is recorded as a coordinator-owned follow-up. The capability's declared user action is to list the Installation's Requirements as one Backlog, its declared success condition is that listRequirements and queueSummary return the current Backlog state with no shortfall, and its owner surface is /v1/requirements -- for which the bounded page plus its cursor is the only way to see a Backlog larger than one page. In the same change, the dogfood tripwire is turned into the assertion it demands: internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go's capBacklogVisibility currently FAILS ON PURPOSE if the second page succeeds, with a message instructing the reader to re-judge the verdict. Replace that inverted assertion with the same full-walk coverage assertion d6 uses, keep the recorded E22-11 history and its date in the comment, and record this specific check as COMPILED AND VETTED BUT NOT EXECUTED, because TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood additionally requires the Provider gate and makes real claude invocations that this task does not authorise.
decisions.rationale: Leaving the tripwire would guarantee a red M5 re-dogfood whose only cause is a stale assertion this task already knows the correct replacement for, and the tripwire's own message asks the task that makes the fact true to supply the judgement. But honesty about execution is not negotiable: the check must be recorded with status skipped and the record's result must be partial rather than passed for the api component, naming the M5 re-dogfood as the gate that executes it. That is also why d6 exists -- the executable emulator-backed HTTP walk means the outcome itself is proven by an executed check, and only the capability VERDICT waits on the re-dogfood.

decisions.decision: Rollback is a single revert of internal/store/firestore/store.go, and nothing else has to be undone. The change writes no document, reads no document it did not already read, alters no stored field, alters no document id, adds no index and changes no wire format: the cursor the route emits is byte-identical before and after (d3), and every document already in Firestore keeps the id it has. A reverted deployment therefore sees exactly the pre-change behaviour, including the 400, with no data left behind to reconcile.
decisions.rationale: Stating this precisely is what makes the change safe to land alone rather than behind a flag. The property that carries it is that the defect was in a QUERY ARGUMENT and not in any persisted representation -- so there is no version of the data that only the new code can read, and no cursor already in a caller's hands that the old code would mis-handle differently than it already does.

decisions.decision: Escalate rather than proceed on any of these: an index turns out to be required (d9); the cross-adapter test cannot be written without asserting an order (d4); making the dogfood tripwire correct requires editing anything in internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go outside capBacklogVisibility; the Firestore emulator cannot be started, in which case the store checks are recorded skipped and the record is partial and the task STOPS rather than reporting a pass (gate rule G7); component-api or component-store-memory turns red for a cause the diff does not explain; or a fix appears to need internal/application/**, internal/reconciler/**, contracts/** or firestore.indexes.json.
decisions.rationale: Each of these is a signal that a different design is being built. The emulator case is called out separately because it is the one failure mode that silently converts this task's central evidence into nothing: the store tests skip when FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST is unset (internal/store/firestore/store_test.go:41-43), so an unwrapped go test ./internal/store/firestore is GREEN while measuring the defect not at all -- which is exactly the shape gate rule G7 forbids counting as a pass.

verification: devbox run --pure -- make component-store-firestore, judged by its own verdict line and never by the shell exit status, green with the Firestore emulator actually started by scripts/firestore-emulator.sh. An emulator-less run of ./internal/store/firestore is NOT acceptable evidence: its cases skip, and a skip is never a pass (gate rule G7).

devbox run --pure -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -race -count=1 -v -run 'TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce|TestTheEventPageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryEventIsCoveredOnce' ./internal/store/firestore, green, and observed to FAIL on the pre-change tree so the test is proven able to see the defect it fixes.

devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestThePageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryRequirementIsCoveredOnce|TestTheEventPageCursorTheCallerWasHandedIsAcceptedByTheNextPageUntilEveryEventIsCoveredOnce' ./internal/store/memory, green under the identical test names.

devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api, green, with the multi-page HTTP walk over the real control-plane binary and the real emulator covering every captured Requirement exactly once.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v -run TestTheBacklogStillRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue ./internal/api, green, with all four rejected shapes producing 400 invalid_request.
devbox run --pure -- make component-store-memory and devbox run --pure -- make component-api, each judged by its own verdict line.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./... green and devbox run --pure -- go vet ./... clean. The full make check is NOT run by the implementer; the coordinator runs it once at integration.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts, green with the three evidence records registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json.

git grep -n 'StartAfter' over the final tree returns exactly three call sites, all in internal/store/firestore/store.go, and none of them concatenates a collection path with a document key; the two paged reads pass the d2 helper's result and ExpiredActiveLeases is unchanged.

go build of internal/api succeeds with the rewritten capBacklogVisibility and devbox run --pure -- go vet ./internal/api is clean, recorded as compiled and vetted but NOT executed, with the M5 re-dogfood named as the gate that executes it.
devbox run --pure -- gitleaks dir .agents --config .gitleaks.toml, run after the evidence commit, clean. Never gitleaks dir .
risks: The store tests skip silently without FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, so an implementer can run ./internal/store/firestore, see green, and have measured nothing. Every store check must be wrapped by scripts/firestore-emulator.sh or by make component-store-firestore, and any skip makes the record partial and stops the task.

The two adapters do not share a total order (d4). A cross-adapter test that asserts raw-id ascending order will pass on memory and fail on Firestore, and the likely reaction is to weaken the walk rather than to drop the order assertion. The test must assert coverage as a multiset and say so in its own comment.

The dogfood tripwire in internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go is rewritten but cannot be executed here. If it is rewritten wrongly, the M5 re-dogfood discovers it. Mitigation: it reuses the same walk shape as the executable d6 assertion, and the check is recorded skipped with the api record's result partial.

internal/reconciler/orphan.go's sweep is silently repaired by this change without any reconciler test observing it, because internal/reconciler tests run on the memory adapter where it already worked. The repair is recorded as a measured consequence, not asserted; a reconciler-level Firestore test would be its own task.

The 400-for-any-unclassified-error default in internal/api's domainError is left in place (d7), so a future storage-side InvalidArgument on any route will again be reported to the caller as a client mistake. Escalated to the coordinator as its own task rather than fixed inside this outcome.

The first-page-only reads at internal/application/allocation.go:603 and release_surface.go:265 consume an adapter-specific order (d4). This task neither changes nor fixes that; recorded so a later reader does not mistake this task's ordering note for a guarantee that the scheduler sees the same candidates on both adapters.
